subject: MSA / Order Form — SLA response tiers, credits & maintenance windows
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@catalysthealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Catalyst Health Legal <legal@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA redlines attached

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the order form. Our legal team attached redlines (see attached Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx) with a few principal asks on the SLA section that we need to resolve before Procurement can approve: 

- Uptime: request explicit 99.95% Monthly Uptime (measured per calendar month) for production endpoints used by our clinical app.
- Maintenance windows: limit to max 4 hours per quarter that may impact availability, with minimum 72 hours advance notice; emergency maintenance must be notified as soon as reasonably practicable.
- P1 / P2 response times: initial response within 15 minutes for P1, mitigation (service restored or workaround) within 1 hour; P2 initial response within 1 hour, mitigation within 8 hours.
- Service credits: propose credits escalate by severity — minimum 10% monthly credit for <99.95% but >99.5%, 25% for <99.5%.
- Measurement & exclusions: require clarity that scheduled maintenance and customer-caused downtime are excluded, and request access to hourly uptime logs / monthly report.

Two things we want to flag: Catalyst will need DocuSign-ready language and a one-page SLA table they can attach to the Order Form. Can you confirm what we can commit to for Hosted vs Dedicated variants? Also include any blackout windows for updates to the KV cache that might affect live traffic.

Appreciate a consolidated response so we can close this week.

Best,
Olivia
Director, Vendor Ops
Catalyst Health

Attachment: Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx (redline comments inline)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Catalyst Health Legal <legal@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA redlines attached

Olivia — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. We reviewed with legal and I pulled Aditya into infra/ops questions. Quick confirmations and open items from our side: 

- Measurement baseline: we generally measure Monthly Uptime Percentage (MUP) over the calendar month for billing/credits. We can share hourly uptime logs and a monthly report via a shared Drive link.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: we typically offer a higher uptime SLA for Dedicated (single-tenant/reserved GPU pool) than our multi-tenant Hosted API. We can propose a dedicated MUP target of 99.95% and hosted target of 99.9% for the services used in your workload — will confirm with CS/infra.
- Maintenance window ask: 72 hours notice is reasonable for planned maintenance. We need to propose a concrete bound; our current standard is up to 2 hours per month maintenance that may affect availability (we can consolidate into <= 8 hours/quarter). Is Catalyst comfortable with 8 hours/quarter?
- P1/P2 timeliness: the 15m / 1h P1 targets are aggressive for a hosted platform — they align with enterprise Dedicated SLAs in some cases. Can you confirm whether you need this for Hosted or only for Dedicated? Also need to align on definitions of P1/P2 (impact to clinical workflows vs non-critical).
- Credits: we can provide a credits matrix but need to align on thresholds and the calculation period. We have a draft credit table attached (redline_summary.xlsx).

Action items: Monica — can you drive legal wording around measurement and exclusions? Aditya — can you comment on maintenance window feasibility and the feasibility of 15m initial response for Dedicated?

Olivia — if you can confirm whether the 15m/1h P1 requirement is for Hosted or Dedicated only, we’ll propose a clean counter and get it to you for DocuSign by Friday.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_summary.xlsx (SLA draft credit matrix and notes)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA redlines attached

Quick technical notes from infra: 

- Maintenance windows: we can support a hard cap of 8 hours/quarter that may impact availability; planned updates will be scheduled with 72h notice. For Dedicated we can push most updates via hotpatching with zero downtime in many cases, so effective impact should be less than the cap.
- P1 response: initial acknowledgement (triage) within 15 minutes is operationally possible for Dedicated with a dedicated on-call rotation and pager; for Hosted (shared) we can commit to 30 minutes for initial response and a 4-hour mitigation SLA for P1 incidents.
- Measurement: our telemetry publishes per-instance hourly availability and aggregate monthly Uptime percentage. We can provide a link to an automated report each month and a raw hourly CSV on request.

One caveat: the 'mitigation' definition needs precision — mitigation = either service restored to normal or a documented short-term workaround reducing customer impact. Full root-cause and remediation timelines are treated separately.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute sync to align definitions if helpful.

—Aditya
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Catalyst Health Legal <legal@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA response tiers, credits & maintenance windows (proposed counter)

Olivia / Catalyst team — thanks for the redlines and for the patience while we pulled internal counsel and SREs together. Below is our proposed counter for the Order Form / SLA table (summary here; full redline PDF and credit matrix attached):

Proposed counters (summary):
- Uptime (Monthly): Dedicated: 99.95% MUP; Hosted: 99.9% MUP. Measurement: calendar month; hourly telemetry available on request.
- Maintenance windows: Planned maintenance that may impact availability limited to 8 hours per calendar quarter; minimum 72 hours notice. Emergency maintenance: Redwood will notify as soon as practicable and will document the reason and estimated impact.
- Incident response / mitigation (P1): Dedicated: initial response within 15 minutes, mitigation target within 1 hour. Hosted: initial response within 30 minutes, mitigation target within 4 hours. P2: initial response within 1 hour, mitigation target within 8 hours. Exact severity definitions attached.
- Service credits: attached SLA-credit-matrix-v2.csv. Example: for Dedicated, failure to meet 99.95% MUP results in tiered credits (5% credit for <99.95% & >=99.5%, 15% for <99.5% & >=99.0%, etc.). We adjusted percentages vs your proposal and included a max cap and exclusion language.
- Exclusions & measurement: scheduled maintenance (as defined above), customer-caused outages, third-party provider outages, and force majeure are excluded. We will provide monthly uptime reports and hourly logs on request; access details in the attached doc.

Next steps: 
1) Monica and Redwood Legal will update the Order Form and SLA appendix with the proposed wording and send a DocuSign-ready file by EOD Friday.
2) Olivia / Catalyst Legal to confirm acceptance or provide a narrow set of items you still want to negotiate (please highlight line numbers).
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 20-minute alignment call to go through definitions and the credit matrix. Proposed times: Fri 10:00–11:00 PT or Mon 09:00–10:00 PT.

Olivia — attaching redline_summary.xlsx and SLA-credit-matrix-v2.csv for your review. If we can get confirmation on the Dedicated vs Hosted scope for the clinical endpoints, we’ll finalize language and route to DocuSign.

Appreciate the collaboration — aiming to close this week.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_summary.xlsx, SLA-credit-matrix-v2.csv
